extracted.intended_audience: writers preparing to apply to Pitch Wars (middle-grade, YA, and adult fiction authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for writers with completed manuscripts who plan to apply to the Pitch Wars mentorship program, covering eligibility, materials, formatting, mentor research, and how to maximize chances during the short three-month mentorship window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program scope and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: It’s a short-term (about 3 months) mentorship program for writers of Middle-grade, YA, and adult fiction. It only opens for a brief period in the early fall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentor/mentee pairs are announced in early November, and the Agent Showcase is in early February. Know the submission open/close dates (example given: opens 9/26/21 and closes 9/30/21 for that year) and be prepared to work intensively for the three months leading up to the Agent Showcase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: manuscript status and allowed types
rubrics_metrics.description: The contest is open to unagented, unpublished manuscripts only. Also, not picture books, novellas, or nonfiction (though some mentors may take graphic novels or memoir).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This program is specifically geared toward writers who have a completed manuscript, preferably one that is already fairly polished. This is not the place to throw your hat in the ring after completing a first draft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to commit and openness to feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: You have to be willing to commit to the process 100% in order to be ready. If you are not ready for real, constructive feedback, or are looking for someone to pat you on the back, don’t bother applying!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentors will give rigorous, potentially overwhelming feedback; mentor/mentee relationships may not always work out and you are not obligated to take their advice, but you must be open to it and prepared to put in substantial work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research mentors and ensure genre fit
rubrics_metrics.description: You need to research the available mentors carefully, to see which ones are taking your genre, and what they are looking for. Read the mentor bios and understand what they are looking for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can only apply to 4, so choose wisely. Do not submit to a mentor that is not in your genre (i.e., if you write fantasy, don’t submit to someone who is only looking for contemporary realistic fiction). Mentors have very specific things they are looking for.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission materials required
rubrics_metrics.description: You will submit your first chapter plus query letter and synopsis by the due date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a mentor is interested they may ask for more chapters before making a decision, so be ready (but DON’T send them with your initial submission). Ensure query and synopsis are compelling as they influence a mentor's interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have a full, revised, polished manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a full, revised, polished manuscript ready. Ideally, one that has been beta-read by somebody else.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the manuscript, query, or synopsis don’t make sense or are not compelling, it won’t help make your case to a possible mentor. The program expects work that can be brought to a high standard in three months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word count must suit genre expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure your manuscript length is within the word count expected for your genre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check genre-specific expectations (word count ranges) before submitting so you don't mismatch with mentor expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading and line-editing quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure it is as free from grammatical and spelling errors and typos as possible - i.e., do a line edit, and proofread.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careless errors signal inability/unwillingness to follow guidelines and may negatively affect mentor interest; polish improves chances when mentors shortlist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow submission guidelines to the letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the submission guidelines, and make sure your submission follows them to the letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentors will be reading hundreds of submissions and will likely shortlist fewer than ten. Don’t lose out because you disregarded the rules or were careless—failure to follow guidelines may cause immediate rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript formatting standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Use standard accepted manuscript formatting: Times New Roman 12 point font; double spaced with one inch margins; page break after each chapter; space down 2-3 lines before each chapter title; include page number, manuscript title, and your name in the header.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhering to standard formatting demonstrates professionalism and makes your submission easy to read; deviations may annoy mentors who review many entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application strategy: choosing mentors
rubrics_metrics.description: You can only apply to 4, so choose wisely!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider mentors actively looking for your genre and those who seek diverse writers; don’t waste slots on clearly unsuitable mentors. Because many mentors look for diverse writers, some applicants may find more suitable mentor options than their four allowed choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not send extra material unless requested
rubrics_metrics.description: If a mentor is interested they may ask for more chapters before making a decision, so be ready (but DON’T send them with your initial submission).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only provide additional requested material upon request; unsolicited extra pages may violate submission rules or be ignored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic expectations about benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: All the mentors are previously-published authors. You get one-on-one attention to you and your manuscript for free, for three months. You get the attention of agents who are eager to see the mentees’ manuscripts because they know they’ve been rigorously worked on and are in top shape.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This offers a strong leg up toward publication but is not a guarantee—many Agent Showcase entries are not chosen by agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance odds and competitiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Honestly, slim. Thousands of writers apply. There are about 75 mentors for each genre, but some work in pairs, so it’s not 75 total. Each mentor or mentor pair takes on one writer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is subjective and mentors shortlist fewer than ten; do not take non-acceptance as blanket rejection of your novel or your writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-rejection next steps and community resources
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are not accepted, do not take it as a blanket rejection of your novel, or of your writing, or of you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Get beta readers, friends, and other support (e.g., in the Twitter sphere by tagging #PitchWars). Keep writing, revising, and submitting to agents; view the experience as one of many opportunities.
